finding.scenario: PostgreSQL positional relation column aliases can rename the restricted knowledge_bases.cos_config column to description. The allowed-column validator accepts description and security predicates still permit the authorized row, exposing stored provider credentials through database_query. Renaming owner/filter columns can also change the meaning of injected predicates.
finding.before: Actual ValidateAndSecureSQL with security defaults, soft delete, hidden KB and authorized scope accepted the crafted query. A network-disabled, tmpfs PostgreSQL16 fixture using the migration column order returned only the fake audit-canary secret. Three permanent relation-alias cases and the predicate-only option test failed before the change; ordinary SELECT result aliases passed.
finding.fix: Reject relation column alias lists whenever column allowlists or canonical security predicates are enabled. Ordinary table aliases and SELECT expression AS output_label remain supported.

validation.result: The same real query now returns validation false, an explanatory detail, and no executable SQL. The real DatabaseQueryTool.Execute route rejects before reading its isolated empty database.

verification_note: The first consumer test asserted the returned error included the tool-result wrapper text; production already rejected correctly. Corrected the fixture to assert the actual returned error and separately the result.Error wrapper; reran full packages successfully.
